t: This is Fenchurch Street, which runs through the City of London's financial district from Aldgate in the east towards Lombard Street and Gracechurch Street. The name means church in the fenny or marshy ground, probably after St Gabriel Fenchurch, destroyed in the Great Fire. Two people are linked to the street. Richard Thomson, an English librarian and antiquarian, was born here in 1794. Monkhouse Davison, a grocer at Davison Newman and Company, died here in 1793. The firm's tea chests were among those thrown into the water in the Boston Tea Party.
